name: Herrenvolk democracy
summary: Herrenvolk democracy is a regime, and the racial-egalitarian ideology behind it, that is democratic for a dominant racial group and tyrannical for subordinate ones. Whites (the 'master race') get the vote, office and equality among themselves, while nonwhites are denied political rights, kept out of citizenship and segregated. The scholarship (van den Berghe, Fredrickson, Vickery, Woodward) places it chiefly in the nineteenth and twentieth century American South and South Africa, and ties the growth of democracy for whites to harsher racial subordination.
scope: The concept coined by Pierre van den Berghe in Race and Racism (1967), as the defining scholarship uses it: Vickery 1974 and Fredrickson (1971, 1981) on the antebellum and post-Reconstruction US South and the Boer republics, Cape politics and Union South Africa. Answers come from the regimes and movements those works describe as Herrenvolk democracy, and from the doctrine they record ('the white man is the equal of every other white man; the Negro is the inferior race'). Later uses of the label for other states (Israel, Liberia) and the related ethnic democracy and ethnocracy models are other subjects.

furtherReading.title: 'Herrenvolk' Democracy and Egalitarianism in South Africa and the U.S. South (Vickery, 1974)
furtherReading.note: The clearest scholarly account of the idea, comparing the US South and South Africa.

furtherReading.title: Our Own Herrenvolk (C. Vann Woodward, 1971)
furtherReading.note: A historian's review explaining how racism and democracy formed a 'strange marriage'.

furtherReading.title: Reflections on the Twenty-Fifth Anniversary of White Supremacy (Fredrickson, 2006)
furtherReading.note: Fredrickson on how he took the concept from van den Berghe and applied it.

missingStatements.text: All members of a country's dominant ethnic group should be equal before the law regardless of wealth.
missingStatements.rationale: Herrenvolk egalitarianism extends equality to everyone inside the dominant group and not to those outside it; class distinctions among whites are denounced.

quotes.text: Herrenvolk egalitarianism can be seen as the extension of equality in political, economic, or other spheres to those within the dominant group but not to those without.
all the white race, however high or low, rich or poor, are equal in the eyes of the law.

notes: Themes searched: franchise and office, segregation and marriage law, racial doctrine, labour (white unions, South African civilised labour policy), economy, immigration, colonial matters. Most statements are null because the scholarship describes a regime type and its racial-political ideology and says nothing on them. Van den Berghe's Race and Racism (1967) and Roediger's Wages of Whiteness were not available as open full texts, so the definition rests on their citation by Vickery, Woodward and Fredrickson.
